text:
Sam: FYI Support ticket #54910 from MediVault. They need streaming responses that include interleaved structured frames (tool_call/tool_result) as separate JSON events — their ingest pipeline consumes each event as it arrives.

support-bot: Ticket created: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/54910 — assigned to Sam. :rotating_light:

Lina: Quick context: customer runs private deployment (on-prem). Their client expects incremental tool_call frames so they can kick off a secure lookup service mid-response. Right now we only emit fn_call at end-of-turn which breaks their flow.

Rashid: Can you paste a minimal example of what they expect vs what they see?

Sam: Example from customer (what they expect):
```json
{"event":"message","text":"Start transfer"}
{"event":"tool_call","name":"check_limits","args":{"acct": "444"}}
{"event":"tool_result","result":{"allowed": true}}
{"event":"message","text":"Proceeding"}
```
What they currently receive: initial message tokens -> final fn_call consolidated after turn. No mid-stream structured frames.

Tara: Engineering note: on Private we run the same token-delta stream as Hosted. Event-level streaming was prototyped (RFC-321) but not GA. For on-prem we also need to consider deployment version skew across controller/agents; changing framing requires orchestration upgrades.

Lina: Customer impact: blocked pilot for secure transfers. They asked for a short-term compatibility path. Business: small pilot ARR but legal requires on-prem, so winning them matters for private offering credibility.

Rashid: Options:
- compatibility shim (targeted for Private + Dedicated): emit a synthetic token frame that contains a single JSON event payload (e.g., escaped JSON line). Pros: no protocol change; minimal client work. Cons: brittle, parsing oddities, edge cases for multi-event turns. Estimate: 1 sprint + QA.
- formal event frames: add "event" frames as first-class streaming frames and update SDKs & agent. Pros: clean, future-proof. Cons: multi-sprint, migration complexity. Estimate: 3-4 sprints.
- hybrid: add opt-in header for "event-mode" in the connection; server will emit event frames only if negotiated. Medium effort: 2 sprints + SDK updates.

Sam: Customer can do a temporary workaround (polling status) but that's insecure and adds latency. They asked if we can do a short-lived patch for their on-prem cluster.

Tara: Risks: privacy (tool args may include PII) — need privacy checklist. Also compatibility with older agents; for Private we need a clear upgrade plan.

Rashid: Proposed canary scope: Private pilot cluster for MediVault only, using shim path behind an opt-in flag in the admin console. Acceptance criteria:
- MediVault receives separate event-delimited frames in the same order as produced by model (msg, tool_call, tool_result, msg).
- No degradation in token throughput for non-opted-in customers.
- Security checklist completed: PII exposure mitigations + audit log entries.
- E2E test exercising an on-prem webhook that consumes per-event JSON.

Lina: Product ask: ship shim to Private clusters first (low blast radius), document the admin opt-in, and begin event-frame RFC work in parallel if we get 3+ customers requesting it.

Sam: Triage decision: create RDW-3180 (customer-54910-event-shim-private). Priority: P2. If MediVault confirms contract hinge, escalate to P1.

Rashid: I'll own the shim prototype and the admin opt-in flag. ETA: prototype in 7 working days, canary in 14.

Tara: I'll schedule a privacy review and confirm agent upgrade constraints.

Lina: I'll notify Sales and Solutions to coordinate the pilot and customer comms.

Sam: Action items:
- RDW-3180 created and linked to ticket.
- Rashid posts design notes and wire diagram by EOD Fri.
- Tara runs privacy checklist and posts outcome.
- Product will track downstream SDK work if we decide to move to formal event frames.

Rashid: tagging @Lina when I post the design. :mailbox_with_mail:
